# #707 — sme-per-entry-files.sh is permanently RED: one entry uses a level-1 undated heading, so its finding is invisible to the index

State: OPEN
Author: rodaddy
Labels: none
Created: 2026-08-10T01:24:51Z
Updated: 2026-08-10T01:24:51Z

---

## What happens

`scripts/done-means/sme-per-entry-files.sh` clause 1 requires every entry file
in `docs/sme/entries/` to carry exactly one finding heading in the
`## [YYYY-MM-DD] Title` form. One file does not:

```
docs/sme/entries/2026-08-08-guards-must-judge-the-operation-not-the-vocabulary.md
```

Its heading is `# A guard that matches vocabulary taxes every lane; judge the
operation` — a level-1 heading with no date prefix — so the check counts 0
finding headings and reports:

```
FAIL  1 entry file(s) do not carry exactly one finding heading
```

Its front matter also uses a different key set from its neighbours
(`scope:`/`severity:`/`status:`/`provenance:` as YAML keys, where other entries
carry those as bold lines in the body).

## Where

`docs/sme/entries/2026-08-08-guards-must-judge-the-operation-not-the-vocabulary.md`,
lines 1-10.

## Proven pre-existing, not lane-introduced

Verified 2026-08-09 by running the check in the untouched primary checkout at
`a45e7d9` (the base of `wip/2026-08-07`):

```
FAIL  1 entry file(s) do not carry exactly one finding heading
      dated entries across docs/sme/entries: 231
      pinned pre-migration baseline:      227
RESULT  RED — 2 clause failure(s)
```

So the base commit already fails this clause. Filed from
`lane/fix-gates-705-706` (#705/#706), which did not touch this file and left it
alone rather than absorbing an unrelated fix into a gate-fixing PR.

## Why it matters

The entry is invisible to `scripts/build-sme-indexes.ts` as a finding, so a
real gotcha-agent lesson about guards matching vocabulary is not reaching the
generated lane file that reviewers read. It also keeps
`sme-per-entry-files.sh` permanently RED, which is the state that trains people
to read a red check as background noise.

## Note on the entry count

The same run shows the base at 231 dated entries against a pinned baseline of
227 — four entries added by earlier lanes without raising
`EXPECTED_ENTRY_COUNT`. `lane/fix-gates-705-706` raised the pin to 232 (its own
single entry plus those four) and announced it in the script and its PR body,
rather than silently absorbing them. If those four should be re-examined rather
than adopted, that is a separate decision and this issue is the place it is
recorded.
